channel.description: The Moscow Times News এর সর্বশেষ খবর

item.title: Kadyrov’s Son Granted Serbian Citizenship Under an Alias – FBK
item.description: Ali Kadyrov, using the alias Ali Ramzanovich Musayev, was naturalized per a decree signed by Serbia’s prime minister and published on July 10, 2025, in the country’s official gazette.

item.title: Zelensky Confirms Ukraine Was Behind Drone Attack on Russian Cargo Ship in Gulf of Finland
item.description: Volodymyr Zelensky said the cargo ship Sparta II and "every vessel with a Russian flag" are legitimate targets for Ukrainian strikes.

item.title: St. Petersburg Offers to Help Build Hanoi Metro as Projects at Home Lag
item.description: Hanoi opened 20 stations from 2021 to 2025, compared with three in St. Petersburg.

item.title: State Duma Approves 2027-29 Budget With Record Military Spending
item.description: Russia plans to raise defense spending to a post-Soviet high next year while cutting civilian programs and increasing taxes.

item.title: Latvia Mulls Possible Border Closure With Russia
item.description: The government discussions come as neighboring Estonia prepares to shutter its checkpoints along the Russian border in response to an alleged Russian sabotage plot against a local drone manufacturer.

item.title: South Korea Says Russian Military Planes Entered Its Air Defense Zone
item.description: The Russian aircraft left the defense zone after South Korean forces took "military measures," including deploying fighter jets, according to South Korea's ministry of national defense.

item.title: Gas Explosion in Altai Region Kills At Least One
item.description: A gas explosion ripped through an apartment building in the Siberian region, killing one and injuring more than a dozen others.

item.title: New Analysis of Rosstat Leak Puts Russian Military Death Toll at 490K or More
item.description: The actual military death toll could exceed 720,000 once delays in registering deaths are taken into account, Meduza and Mediazona estimated.

item.title: Murmansk Governor Arrested in Corruption Probe
item.description: Andrei Chibis is the first sitting Russian governor to be arrested since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

item.title: Drone Alerts Are Disrupting Flights Across Russia. Foreign Airlines Keep Flying Anyway.
item.description: Even with repeated airport restrictions, some international airlines find that flying to Russia remains too lucrative to give up.

item.title: Moscow Summons Estonian Diplomat Over Border Closure
item.description: Russia’s Foreign Ministry warned that the planned border closure would backfire against Estonia and Europe more broadly.

item.title: Who Is Tatyana Kim, the Wildberries CEO Who Just Stepped Down?
item.description: Kim's sanctioning by the EU and resignation from the company she helped build cap a precipitous fall from the top of Russia's business world.

item.title: A Just Russia Party Leader Sergei Mironov Appears in Public Months After Unexplained Injury
item.description: Mironov stopped appearing in public in late August, with party officials explaining at the time that he had suffered a “minor injury” during a work trip and was under medical supervision.

item.title: Russian Government Earmarks $576Mln to Build Rail Ferries Supplying Kaliningrad Region
item.description: The exclave has grown increasingly reliant on sea freight cargo after Lithuania restricted the movement of some goods through its territory.

item.title: Kremlin Dismisses Reports About Alleged Nuclear-Armed Satellite Launch
item.description: German media reported that Western intelligence agencies believe Russia plans to launch a nuclear-armed satellite called Sputnik-S as early as December 2026.
